title: Concordanza dei tempi e discorso indiretto

concepts.title: Sequence of tenses with the indicative (future in the past)
concepts.rule: When the main verb is in a past tense (ha detto, disse, pensavo, sapevo), an action that was still in the future from that past viewpoint goes into the condizionale passato: Ha detto che sarebbe venuto. Never the condizionale presente (~~verrebbe~~), even though English says 'would come'.
assessment: Uses the condizionale passato for a future action seen from a past viewpoint (Ha detto che sarebbe venuto)
Avoids the English calque 'would + verb' → condizionale presente after a past main verb
Chooses imperfetto for simultaneity and trapassato for anteriority after a past main verb
Keeps the futuro after a present main verb (Dice che verrà)
Forms the condizionale passato with the right auxiliary and participle agreement

lesson.intro: "He said he **would** come" looks like a simple conditional in English, so English speakers say ~~Ha detto che verrebbe~~. Italian sees it differently: the coming was *future* from the moment he spoke, and a future seen from the past is expressed with the **condizionale passato**: *Ha detto che **sarebbe venuto***. This is one of the most frequent errors even at C1, and one of the most noticeable to Italian ears.

rules.title: Future in the past = condizionale passato
rules.text: After a past main verb (*ha detto, disse, diceva, aveva detto, pensavo, sapevo, ero sicuro, mi aveva promesso…*), a later action uses *avrebbe / sarebbe* + past participle. It doesn't matter whether the action then happened or not, or even whether it is still in the future today.

examples.it: Marco ha detto che **sarebbe venuto** alle otto.
examples.en: Marco said he would come at eight.

examples.it: Sapevo che **avresti capito**.
examples.en: I knew you would understand.

examples.it: Mi avevano promesso che mi **avrebbero richiamato**, ma non l'hanno fatto.
examples.en: They'd promised they would call me back, but they didn't.

rules.title: The full picture: before, same time, after
rules.text: With a **present** main verb, Italian uses the normal tenses. With a **past** main verb, everything moves one step back: simultaneity → *imperfetto*, anteriority → *trapassato prossimo*, posteriority → *condizionale passato*.

examples.it: Ha detto che **era** stanca.
examples.en: She said she was tired (at that moment).

examples.it: Ha detto che **era già partita**.
examples.en: She said she had already left.

examples.it: Ha detto che **sarebbe partita** il giorno dopo.
examples.en: She said she would leave the next day.

rules.title: Forming the condizionale passato
rules.text: Condizionale presente of *avere* or *essere* + past participle. Verbs that take *essere* (andare, venire, partire, tornare, diventare, reflexives…) agree with the subject: *Le ragazze hanno detto che sarebbero **tornate** presto.*

rules.title: What you'll hear in conversation
rules.text: In everyday speech Italians often use the **imperfetto** for the future in the past: *Ha detto che veniva*. It's fine in conversation, but in writing and careful speech use the condizionale passato. If the event is still ahead of us now, the **futuro** is also heard (*Mi ha detto ieri che verrà domani*). The condizionale passato is always correct.

examples.it: Ha detto che veniva. (colloquial)
examples.en: He said he was coming.

examples.it: Ha detto che sarebbe venuto. (standard)
examples.en: He said he would come.

mistakes.why: English 'would come' is a future in the past here, not a condition. *Verrebbe* means 'he would come (if…)'.
After a past main verb the future becomes condizionale passato.

mistakes.wrong: Pensavo che il film finirebbe presto.
mistakes.right: Pensavo che il film sarebbe finito presto.
mistakes.why: Same calque: 'would end' seen from the past → *sarebbe finito*.

mistakes.wrong: Le ragazze hanno detto che sarebbero venuti.
mistakes.right: Le ragazze hanno detto che sarebbero venute.
mistakes.why: With *essere* the participle agrees with the subject: feminine plural → *venute*.

mistakes.wrong: Ha detto che sarebbe stata stanca.
mistakes.why: If the state was at the same time as the speaking, use the imperfetto, not the condizionale passato.

tips: Alarm bell: past main verb + English 'would' = *avrebbe / sarebbe* + participle.
Ask yourself: was it **before**, **during** or **after** the moment of speaking? → trapassato, imperfetto, condizionale passato.
You'll hear *Ha detto che veniva* all the time. Understand it, but write *sarebbe venuto*.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Marco ha detto che ___ (venire) alla festa, ma poi non si è fatto vedere.

traps.why: 'Would come' after a past main verb is a future in the past: condizionale **passato**, *sarebbe venuto*. *Verrebbe* means 'would come (if…)'.
The main verb is past (*ha detto*) and the party is over: the future becomes *sarebbe venuto*.
Very common in conversation. In writing and careful speech use the condizionale passato: *sarebbe venuto*.
*Venire* takes *essere*: *sarebbe venuto*.

exercises.explanation: Past main verb + later action → condizionale passato: **sarebbe venuto**.
exercises.en: Marco said he'd come to the party, but then he didn't show up.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Mi avevi promesso che mi ___ (chiamare) appena arrivato.

traps.why: English 'you would call' → after a past main verb Italian needs *avresti chiamato*.
The promise is in the past (*avevi promesso*), so the future becomes condizionale passato.
Colloquial. The standard form is *avresti chiamato*.

exercises.explanation: Promise in the past → future in the past → **avresti chiamato**.
exercises.en: You had promised you'd call me as soon as you arrived.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Le previsioni dicevano che ___ (piovere) tutto il weekend, e invece c'era il sole.

traps.why: Seen from the past (*dicevano*), a later event takes the condizionale **passato**: *sarebbe (avrebbe) piovuto*.
The weekend is over: from a past viewpoint use *sarebbe piovuto*.
In speech you may hear this, but here it's ambiguous: it sounds like 'it was raining (at that moment)'. Use *sarebbe piovuto*.

exercises.explanation: Future in the past → condizionale passato. Weather verbs accept both auxiliaries: **sarebbe / avrebbe piovuto**.
exercises.en: The forecast said it would rain all weekend, but it was sunny.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Ero sicura che i ragazzi ___ (capire) subito.

traps.why: The English 'would understand' tempts you to use the present conditional. After *ero sicura*, the later event is *avrebbero capito*.
Past main verb → future becomes condizionale passato.
*Essere sicuro* expresses certainty, so no subjunctive. For a later action: *avrebbero capito*.

exercises.explanation: *Ero sicura che* (certainty, past) + later action → **avrebbero capito**.
exercises.en: I was sure the boys would understand straight away.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct form.
exercises.prompt: Nel 2015 Lucia mi scrisse che ___ a Roma l'anno seguente.

optionWhy.0: Calque of 'she would move'. Future in the past = condizionale **passato**.
optionWhy.2: The main verb is past (*scrisse*): the future must shift to *si sarebbe trasferita*.
optionWhy.3: Passato prossimo describes something before the writing, but she moved *the following year*.

exercises.explanation: *Scrisse* (past) + 'the following year' (later) → **si sarebbe trasferita**.
exercises.en: In 2015 Lucia wrote to me that she would move to Rome the following year.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct form. Watch the tense of the main verb.
exercises.prompt: Luca dice sempre che domani ___ in palestra, ma non ci va mai.

optionWhy.0: The main verb is **present** (*dice*), so no shift: a future stays a future, *andrà*.
optionWhy.2: *Andrebbe* is a conditional ('would go if…'). With *dice* + *domani* you need the future.
optionWhy.3: *Dire che* reporting a statement takes the indicative, not the subjunctive.

exercises.explanation: Contrast item: with a present main verb, no shift. Future → **andrà**.
exercises.en: Luca always says he'll go to the gym tomorrow, but he never goes.

exercises.instruction: Before, same time or after? Complete with the correct form.
exercises.prompt: Quando l'ho chiamata, Anna mi ha detto che ___ (essere) troppo stanca per uscire.

traps.why: She was tired **at the time** she spoke (simultaneity): imperfetto *era*, not condizionale passato.
Simultaneous state in the past → imperfetto *era*.
*Dire che* reporting a statement takes the indicative: *era*.

exercises.explanation: Simultaneity with a past main verb → **imperfetto**: *era*.
exercises.en: When I called her, Anna told me she was too tired to go out.

exercises.instruction: Before, same time or after? Complete with the correct form.
exercises.prompt: Il tecnico ci disse che qualcuno ___ (manomettere) il contatore prima del suo arrivo.

traps.why: *Prima del suo arrivo* = **before**: anteriority in the past → trapassato *aveva manomesso*.
With a past main verb (*disse*), an earlier action goes into the trapassato: *aveva manomesso*.

exercises.explanation: Anteriority with a past main verb → **trapassato prossimo**: *aveva manomesso*.
exercises.en: The technician told us that someone had tampered with the meter before he arrived.

exercises.instruction: Translate into Italian.
exercises.prompt: She told me she would call me later.
answers: [Lei] mi (ha detto|disse) che mi avrebbe (chiamato|chiamata|richiamato|richiamata|telefonato) (più tardi|dopo)

traps.why: 'Would call' after a past main verb = future in the past → *avrebbe chiamato*.
Past main verb (*mi ha detto*): the future shifts to *avrebbe chiamato*.

exercises.explanation: *Mi ha detto* (past) + later action → **mi avrebbe chiamato**.
exercises.en: She told me she would call me later.

exercises.instruction: Translate into Italian (informal 'you').
exercises.prompt: I knew you would understand.

traps.why: The classic calque. 'Would understand' seen from the past → *avresti capito*.
*Sapevo* is past, so the future becomes *avresti capito*.
*Sapevo che capivi* means 'I knew you understood' (same time). For 'would understand' use *avresti capito*.
*Sapere* states a certainty: no subjunctive. Use *avresti capito*.

exercises.explanation: *Sapevo* + later action → **avresti capito**.
exercises.en: I knew you would understand.

exercises.instruction: Report it in the past, starting with 'Ha detto che…'.
exercises.prompt: Dice che arriverà alle otto.
answers: Ha detto che sarebbe (arrivato|arrivata) alle otto

traps.why: Future → condizionale **passato** after *ha detto*: *sarebbe arrivato*.
The main verb is now past, so the future must shift: *sarebbe arrivato*.
*Arrivare* takes *essere*: *sarebbe arrivato/a*.

exercises.explanation: *Dice che arriverà* → *Ha detto che **sarebbe arrivato***.
exercises.en: He said he would arrive at eight.

exercises.instruction: Rewrite starting with 'Eravamo convinti che…'.
exercises.prompt: Il concerto finirà tardi.
answers: Eravamo convinti che il concerto sarebbe finito tardi

traps.why: 'Would end' from a past viewpoint → *sarebbe finito*.
Past main verb → the future becomes condizionale passato.
Intransitive *finire* (the concert ends) takes *essere*: *sarebbe finito*.

traps.match: Eravamo convinti che il concerto finisse tardi
traps.why: Also heard: the congiuntivo imperfetto can carry a future meaning after opinion verbs. The condizionale passato *sarebbe finito* is the clearest choice for 'would end'.

exercises.explanation: Past opinion verb + later event → **sarebbe finito**.
exercises.en: We were convinced the concert would end late.

exercises.instruction: Put the words in order.
exercises.prompt: They assured us the parcel would arrive on Monday.
answers: Ci hanno assicurato che il pacco sarebbe arrivato lunedì
Ci hanno assicurato che lunedì il pacco sarebbe arrivato
exercises.explanation: *Ci hanno assicurato* (past) + later action → *sarebbe arrivato*. The object pronoun *ci* comes before the auxiliary.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct form.
exercises.prompt: Giorgio pensava che noi ___ in ritardo, e invece siamo arrivati puntualissimi.

optionWhy.0: Calque of 'we would arrive'. From a past viewpoint use the condizionale passato.
optionWhy.2: *Pensava* is past: the future shifts to *saremmo arrivati*.
optionWhy.3: Indicative passato prossimo states a fact, and the arrival was *after* his thought.

exercises.explanation: Past opinion + later event → **saremmo arrivati**.
exercises.en: Giorgio thought we'd be late, but we arrived bang on time.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form. Watch the agreement.
exercises.prompt: Le ragazze avevano detto che ___ (tornare) prima di mezzanotte.

traps.why: With *essere*, the participle agrees with *le ragazze*: *tornate*.
'Would come back' from a past viewpoint → *sarebbero tornate*.
*Tornare* takes *essere*.

exercises.explanation: Future in the past, essere-verb, feminine plural → **sarebbero tornate**.
exercises.en: The girls had said they would be back before midnight.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Le mie sorelle mi avevano giurato che non ___ (dire) niente a nessuno.

traps.why: A sworn promise in the past about later behaviour → *avrebbero detto*.
*Avevano giurato* is past: the future becomes condizionale passato.
Transitive *dire* takes *avere*: *avrebbero detto*.

exercises.explanation: Promise in the past → **avrebbero detto**.
exercises.en: My sisters had sworn they wouldn't say anything to anyone.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Nel 1990 nessuno immaginava che quel ragazzino un giorno ___ (diventare) presidente.

traps.why: 'Would become' seen from 1990 → condizionale passato *sarebbe diventato*.
The main verb is past: *sarebbe diventato*.
Also possible after a negated *immaginare*, but *sarebbe diventato* makes the 'later' meaning explicit and is the preferred form.
*Diventare* takes *essere*.

exercises.explanation: 'Would one day become' from a past viewpoint → **sarebbe diventato**.
exercises.en: In 1990 nobody imagined that little boy would one day become president.

exercises.instruction: Say it in Italian.
exercises.prompt: A friend asks why you look surprised that Paolo isn't here. Say: "He told me he would come at nine."
answers: [Mi] (ha detto|aveva detto) che sarebbe (venuto|arrivato|passato) alle nove

traps.why: 'Would come' after *mi ha detto* → *sarebbe venuto*.
Nine o'clock has passed and the main verb is past: *sarebbe venuto*.

exercises.explanation: *Mi ha detto che **sarebbe venuto** alle nove.*
exercises.en: He told me he would come at nine.

exercises.instruction: Write 40–80 words in Italian.
exercises.prompt: Tell the story of a promise someone made to you that they didn't keep. What did they say they would do? What did you think would happen?

rubric.label: Uses the condizionale passato for a future in the past
rubric.hint: Use *avrebbe / sarebbe* + participle: *mi aveva detto che sarebbe venuto*.

rubric.label: Uses a past reporting or thinking verb
anyOf: \b(ha detto|aveva detto|disse|ha promesso|aveva promesso|promise|ha giurato|aveva giurato|ha assicurato|aveva assicurato|pensavo|credevo|ero sicur[oa]|sapevo)\b
rubric.hint: Start from a past verb: *mi aveva promesso che…*, *pensavo che…*

rubric.label: Avoids the 'would' calque (present conditional after a past verb)
rubric.hint: After *ha detto che*, not *verrebbe* but *sarebbe venuto*.

exercises.model: L'anno scorso il mio vicino mi aveva promesso che mi avrebbe aiutato a traslocare. Mi aveva detto che sarebbe venuto alle otto con il furgone di suo fratello. Io ero sicuro che sarebbe stato puntuale, e invece alle dieci non era ancora arrivato. Alla fine mi ha scritto che il furgone si era rotto. Ho dovuto fare tutto da solo!
exercises.explanation: Past reporting verb + later action → condizionale passato.

concepts.title: Sequence of tenses with the subjunctive
concepts.rule: The tense of the subjunctive depends on the main verb and on time relation. Present/future main verb → congiuntivo presente (same time/after) or passato (before). Past or conditional main verb → congiuntivo imperfetto (same time) or trapassato (before); after a past main verb a later action takes the condizionale passato.
assessment: Chooses present or past subjunctive after a present main verb according to time relation
Shifts to imperfect or pluperfect subjunctive after a past main verb
Uses the imperfect subjunctive after a conditional main verb (vorrei che, bisognerebbe che)
Uses the condizionale passato for posteriority after a past main verb
Uses the imperfect subjunctive for a past state or habit after a present main verb

lesson.intro: Choosing *that* a subjunctive is needed is B2; choosing *which* subjunctive is C1. English barely changes its verb ("I think / thought she **is / was** right"), but Italian runs a strict grid: the **main verb's tense** and the **time relation** (before, same time, after) decide the form. Get it right and your Italian immediately sounds educated; get it wrong and *Vorrei che tu venga* jars on every native ear.

rules.title: The grid
rules.text: Find the main verb's tense (row), then ask: did the action in the *che*-clause happen before, at the same time as, or after it (column)?

head: Main clause
Before
Same time
After
rows: Any past tense: *Pensavo / Ho pensato / Pensai che…*

rules.title: Present main verb
rules.text: Same time or later → congiuntivo presente. Earlier (a completed event) → congiuntivo passato.

examples.it: Penso che Giulia **sia** a casa.
examples.en: I think Giulia is at home.

examples.it: Penso che Giulia **sia partita** ieri.
examples.en: I think Giulia left yesterday.

examples.it: È probabile che domani **nevichi**.
examples.en: It'll probably snow tomorrow.

rules.title: Past main verb
rules.text: Same time → congiuntivo imperfetto. Earlier → congiuntivo trapassato. Later → condizionale passato (after wish verbs like *volere, sperare*, the imperfetto is normal for later actions too: *Volevo che venissi*).

examples.it: Pensavo che Giulia **fosse** a casa.
examples.en: I thought Giulia was at home.

examples.it: Pensavo che Giulia **fosse partita** il giorno prima.
examples.en: I thought Giulia had left the day before.

examples.it: Pensavo che Giulia **sarebbe partita** il giorno dopo.
examples.en: I thought Giulia would leave the next day.

examples.it: Volevo che tu mi **dicessi** la verità.
examples.en: I wanted you to tell me the truth.

rules.title: Conditional main verb
rules.text: *Vorrei, preferirei, sarebbe meglio, bisognerebbe, mi piacerebbe che* take the **congiuntivo imperfetto**, never the presente. *Avrei voluto che* takes the imperfetto or, for a completed past event, the trapassato.

examples.it: Vorrei che tu **venissi** con me.
examples.en: I'd like you to come with me.

examples.it: Bisognerebbe che il governo **intervenisse**.
examples.en: The government ought to step in.

examples.it: Avrei voluto che tu **venissi / fossi venuto** alla festa.
examples.en: I would have liked you to come to the party.

rules.title: Present main verb, past state or habit
rules.text: When a present main verb comments on a past **state or repeated action** (not a single completed event), use the congiuntivo **imperfetto**: *Credo che da bambino **fosse** molto timido.* Compare the single event: *Credo che ieri **sia uscito** presto.*

examples.it: Si dice che da giovane **suonasse** la chitarra nei locali.
examples.en: They say he used to play guitar in clubs when he was young.

examples.it: Mi dispiace che ieri tu **abbia perso** il treno.
examples.en: I'm sorry you missed the train yesterday.

mistakes.wrong: Vorrei che tu venga con me.
mistakes.right: Vorrei che tu venissi con me.
mistakes.why: A conditional main verb always takes the congiuntivo imperfetto.

mistakes.right: Pensavo che sarebbe arrivato il giorno dopo.
mistakes.why: A later action after a past main verb takes the condizionale passato. The trapassato means 'had arrived'.

mistakes.wrong: Credevo che tu sia a casa.
mistakes.right: Credevo che tu fossi a casa.
mistakes.why: Past main verb → congiuntivo imperfetto for same time.
Past main verb + earlier action → congiuntivo trapassato.

tips: Two questions, every time: 1) Is the main verb present, past or conditional? 2) Before, same time or after?
*Vorrei che* + imperfetto is a fixed reflex: *vorrei che tu fossi, venissi, sapessi*.
In speech you'll hear *Pensavo che era…* (indicative). Write *fosse*.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct subjunctive form.
exercises.prompt: Penso che Giulia ___ (partire) ieri sera.

traps.why: The main verb is present (*penso*): an earlier event takes the congiuntivo **passato**, *sia partita*.
*Penso che* needs the subjunctive: *sia partita*.
*Partire* takes *essere*: the participle agrees with Giulia → *partita*.

exercises.explanation: Present main verb + earlier event → congiuntivo passato: **sia partita**.
exercises.en: I think Giulia left last night.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct subjunctive form.
exercises.prompt: Pensavo che Giulia ___ (essere) a casa.

traps.why: The main verb is past (*pensavo*): same time → congiuntivo **imperfetto**, *fosse*.
Very common in speech, but standard Italian needs the subjunctive after *pensare che*: *fosse*.

exercises.explanation: Past main verb + same time → **fosse**.
exercises.en: I thought Giulia was at home.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct subjunctive form.
exercises.prompt: Credevo che i bambini ___ (cenare) prima del nostro arrivo.

traps.why: *Credevo* is past: an earlier event takes the congiuntivo **trapassato**, *avessero cenato*.
*Prima del nostro arrivo* = before. Before + past main verb → *avessero cenato*.
*Credere che* takes the subjunctive: *avessero cenato*.

exercises.explanation: Past main verb + earlier event → congiuntivo trapassato: **avessero cenato**.
exercises.en: I thought the children had eaten before we arrived.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct subjunctive form.
exercises.prompt: Vorrei che tu mi ___ (ascoltare) almeno una volta.

traps.why: *Vorrei* is conditional: it always takes the congiuntivo **imperfetto**, *ascoltassi*.
No conditional after *che* here: *vorrei che* + congiuntivo imperfetto.

exercises.explanation: Conditional main verb → congiuntivo imperfetto: **ascoltassi**.
exercises.en: I wish you'd listen to me for once.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form.
exercises.prompt: È probabile che domani ___ (nevicare) in montagna.

traps.why: *È probabile* is present: a later event takes the congiuntivo **presente**, *nevichi*.
After a present main verb the future indicative is also used for later events, especially in speech. *Nevichi* is the more formal choice.
*È probabile che* takes the subjunctive.

exercises.explanation: Present main verb + later event → congiuntivo presente **nevichi** (or futuro *nevicherà*).
exercises.en: It'll probably snow in the mountains tomorrow.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct subjunctive form.
exercises.prompt: Mi sembrava strano che Marta non ___ (laurearsi) ancora.

traps.why: *Mi sembrava* is past: an earlier (non-)event takes the trapassato, *si fosse laureata*.
*Non… ancora* refers to something that should already have happened: anteriority → *si fosse laureata*.
Reflexive verbs take *essere*: agree with Marta → *laureata*.

exercises.explanation: Past main verb + anteriority → **si fosse laureata**.
exercises.en: It seemed strange to me that Marta hadn't graduated yet.

exercises.instruction: Choose ALL the correct options (more than one may be right).
exercises.prompt: Avrei voluto che tu ___ con noi ieri sera.

optionWhy.0: A conditional main verb never takes the congiuntivo presente.
optionWhy.2: Also correct: the trapassato stresses the completed event ('that you had come').

exercises.explanation: *Avrei voluto che* + congiuntivo imperfetto (**venissi**) or trapassato (**fossi venuto**).
exercises.en: I would have liked you to come with us last night.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct subjunctive form.
exercises.prompt: Bisognerebbe che il governo ___ (intervenire) subito.

traps.why: *Bisognerebbe* is conditional → congiuntivo **imperfetto**, *intervenisse*.
*Bisognerebbe che* needs the subjunctive, not the conditional.

exercises.explanation: Conditional main clause → **intervenisse**.
exercises.en: The government ought to step in immediately.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct subjunctive form.
exercises.prompt: Mi dispiace che ieri tu ___ (perdere) il treno.

traps.why: The main verb is present (*mi dispiace*): a single earlier event takes the congiuntivo **passato**, *abbia perso*.
Missing a train is a single completed event, not a state or habit: *abbia perso*.
Emotion (*mi dispiace che*) → subjunctive.

exercises.explanation: Present main verb + single earlier event → **abbia perso**.
exercises.en: I'm sorry you missed the train yesterday.

exercises.instruction: Present main verb, but a past habit: complete with the correct form.
exercises.prompt: Si dice che da giovane il nonno ___ (suonare) la chitarra ogni sera nei locali.

traps.why: *Ogni sera* describes a past **habit**: after a present main verb, past habits and states take the congiuntivo imperfetto, *suonasse*.
*Da giovane* places it in the past: *suonasse*.
*Si dice che* (hearsay) takes the subjunctive in standard Italian: *suonasse*.

exercises.explanation: Present main verb + past habit → congiuntivo imperfetto: **suonasse**.
exercises.en: They say Grandpa used to play guitar in clubs every night when he was young.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form (more than one may be possible).
exercises.prompt: Pensavo che il treno ___ (partire) più tardi, e invece l'ho perso.

traps.why: *Pensavo* is past: no congiuntivo presente. Use *sarebbe partito* (later) or *partisse* (scheduled time).
'Would leave' from a past viewpoint → *sarebbe partito*, not the present conditional.
The trapassato means 'had (already) left', which is the opposite of the meaning here.

exercises.explanation: After a past main verb, a later event → **sarebbe partito** (condizionale passato); *partisse* is also natural for a timetable seen as simultaneous.
exercises.en: I thought the train would leave later, but I missed it.

exercises.instruction: Translate into Italian (informal 'you').
exercises.prompt: I wanted you to tell me the truth.
answers: Volevo che [tu] mi dicessi la verità

traps.why: *Volevo* is past → congiuntivo imperfetto, *dicessi*.
*Volere che* always takes the subjunctive: *dicessi*.
Different subjects (I wanted, you tell), so English 'want you to' becomes *volere che* + subjunctive.

exercises.explanation: *Volevo che* + congiuntivo imperfetto: **dicessi**.
exercises.en: I wanted you to tell me the truth.

exercises.instruction: Translate into Italian.
exercises.prompt: I'm afraid they've already left.
answers: (Temo|Ho paura) che [loro] siano già (partiti|partite|usciti|uscite|andati via|andate via)
(Temo|Ho paura) che se ne siano già (andati|andate)

traps.why: *Temo* is present: an earlier event takes the congiuntivo passato, *siano partiti*.
Fear (*temo che*) → subjunctive: *siano partiti*.
*Partire / andare via* take *essere*: *siano partiti*.

exercises.explanation: Present main verb + earlier event → **siano partiti**.
exercises.en: I'm afraid they've already left.

exercises.instruction: Translate into Italian (informal 'you').
exercises.prompt: It would be better if you came tomorrow.

traps.why: *Sarebbe meglio* is conditional → congiuntivo imperfetto, *venissi*.
No conditional after *se* / *che* here: *venissi*.
*Sarebbe meglio che* needs the subjunctive.

exercises.explanation: Conditional main clause → **venissi**.
exercises.en: It would be better if you came tomorrow.

exercises.instruction: Put the main verb in the past: start with 'Speravo che…'.
exercises.prompt: Spero che tu abbia capito.

traps.why: After a past main verb the congiuntivo passato becomes trapassato: *avessi capito*.
The understanding comes *before* the hoping (anteriority): *avessi capito*.

exercises.explanation: Passato → trapassato when the main verb moves to the past: **avessi capito**.
exercises.en: I hoped you had understood.

exercises.instruction: Rewrite starting with 'Era impossibile che…'.
exercises.prompt: È impossibile che lui lo sappia già.
answers: Era impossibile che [lui] lo sapesse già

traps.why: Past main verb → congiuntivo imperfetto: *sapesse*.
*Era impossibile che* still needs the subjunctive.
Third person (lui): *sapesse*.

exercises.explanation: Present → imperfect subjunctive when the main verb is past: **sapesse**.
exercises.en: It was impossible that he already knew.

exercises.instruction: Rewrite starting with 'Credevo che…' (the arrival is later than the believing).
exercises.prompt: Paolo arriverà presto.
answers: Credevo che Paolo sarebbe arrivato presto

traps.why: Past main verb: no congiuntivo presente. Later action → *sarebbe arrivato*.
'Would arrive' from a past viewpoint → condizionale passato.
Also heard: the congiuntivo imperfetto can express a later action. *Sarebbe arrivato* makes posteriority explicit.

traps.match: Credevo che Paolo fosse arrivato presto
traps.why: *Fosse arrivato* = 'had arrived' (before). The arrival is later: *sarebbe arrivato*.

exercises.explanation: Past main verb + later event → **sarebbe arrivato**.
exercises.en: I thought Paolo would arrive soon.

exercises.instruction: Put the words in order.
exercises.prompt: I would have preferred them to tell me straight away.
answers: Avrei preferito che me lo dicessero subito
exercises.explanation: Conditional main verb → imperfetto *dicessero*; the combined pronoun *me lo* goes before the verb.

exercises.instruction: Say it in Italian.
exercises.prompt: A colleague says the meeting is today. Reply: "I thought it was on Thursday."

traps.why: You'll hear *pensavo che era*, but the standard form is *pensavo che fosse*.
*Pensavo* is past → *fosse*.

exercises.explanation: *Pensavo (che) fosse giovedì.* Dropping *che* after *pensavo / credevo* is very natural.
exercises.en: I thought it was on Thursday.

exercises.instruction: Write 50–90 words in Italian.
exercises.prompt: Before you started a new job, school or city, what did you expect? Describe at least three expectations that turned out to be wrong (Pensavo che…, Credevo che…, Speravo che…, Non immaginavo che…).

rubric.label: Uses a past opinion/hope verb + che
Uses the congiuntivo imperfetto or trapassato
rubric.hint: After a past main verb: *fosse, avesse, potessi, ci fossero*…

rubric.label: Uses the condizionale passato for a later expectation

exercises.model: Prima di trasferirmi a Milano pensavo che la città fosse grigia e fredda, e credevo che la gente non avesse mai tempo per parlare. Speravo che trovare casa sarebbe stato facile, e invece ci ho messo tre mesi! Non immaginavo che ci fossero così tanti parchi, né che i colleghi mi avrebbero invitato a cena già la prima settimana.
exercises.explanation: Past main verb → imperfetto / trapassato subjunctive; later events → condizionale passato.

concepts.title: Reported speech (discorso indiretto)
concepts.rule: With a past reporting verb, tenses shift back (presente → imperfetto, passato prossimo → trapassato, futuro → condizionale passato), persons and possessives change, and time/place words shift (qui → lì, domani → il giorno dopo). Commands become di + infinitive (or che + congiuntivo); yes/no questions are introduced by se.
assessment: Shifts tenses correctly when the reporting verb is past
Keeps tenses unchanged when the reporting verb is present
Changes pronouns, possessives and deictics (qui → lì, domani → il giorno dopo)
Reports commands with di + infinitive or che + congiuntivo imperfetto
Reports questions with se or the question word, with indicative or subjunctive

lesson.intro: Reporting what someone said is everyday C1 business: gossip, meetings, news, emails. English shifts tenses too, but Italian adds its own twists: 'would' becomes *condizionale passato*, commands turn into *di* + infinitive, and questions may go into the subjunctive. And don't forget to move the pointers: *qui* becomes *lì* and *domani* becomes *il giorno dopo*.

rules.title: Present reporting verb: no tense shift
rules.text: With *dice, scrive, racconta, chiede* (present), only persons change: «Sono stanca» → *Dice che **è** stanca.* «Partirò domani» → *Dice che **partirà** domani.*

examples.it: Luca dice che verrà anche lui.
examples.en: Luca says he'll come too.

rules.title: Past reporting verb: tenses move back
rules.text: With *ha detto, disse, diceva, aveva detto, ha chiesto…*, the tenses of the original sentence move one step back.

head: Direct speech
Reported (past reporting verb)
rows: congiuntivo passato: «Spero che tu abbia capito»
congiuntivo trapassato: *che sperava che avessi capito*

rules.title: Persons, possessives, time and place
rules.text: Change the pointers to fit the new speaker, place and time. Time words shift only if the time has changed: if you report on the same day, *domani* is still *domani*.

head: Direct
Reported
rows: il giorno dopo / l'indomani / il giorno seguente

rules.title: Commands
rules.text: An imperative becomes **di + infinitive** (most common) or **che + congiuntivo imperfetto** (more formal). Negative: *di non* + infinitive. Pronouns attach to the infinitive.

examples.it: «Chiamami!» → Mi ha detto **di chiamarlo**.
examples.en: He told me to call him.

examples.it: «Non toccate niente!» → Ci ha detto **di non toccare** niente / **che non toccassimo** niente.
examples.en: She told us not to touch anything.

rules.title: Questions
rules.text: Yes/no questions → **se**. Wh-questions keep the question word. After a past reporting verb the verb shifts back and can be indicative (everyday) or subjunctive (formal, written).

examples.it: «Hai fame?» → Mi ha chiesto **se avevo / avessi** fame.
examples.en: She asked me if I was hungry.

examples.it: «Dove abiti?» → Mi ha chiesto **dove abitavo / abitassi**.
examples.en: He asked me where I lived.

mistakes.wrong: Mi ha detto che verrebbe domani.
mistakes.right: Mi ha detto che sarebbe venuto il giorno dopo.
mistakes.why: Future → condizionale passato; and *domani* shifts if you're reporting on a different day.

mistakes.wrong: Mi ha detto che chiudo la porta.
mistakes.right: Mi ha detto di chiudere la porta.

mistakes.wrong: Mi ha chiesto che avevo fame.
mistakes.right: Mi ha chiesto se avevo fame.
mistakes.why: Reported yes/no questions are introduced by *se* ('if/whether'), not *che*.

mistakes.wrong: Luisa disse che era qui da un'ora.
mistakes.right: Luisa disse che era lì da un'ora.
mistakes.why: *Qui* refers to the original speaker's place: in reported speech it usually becomes *lì / là*.

mistakes.wrong: Marco mi ha chiesto di chiamarmi.
mistakes.right: Marco mi ha chiesto di chiamarlo.
mistakes.why: «Chiamami» = call **him** (Marco): the pronoun must change to *lo*.

tips: Three checks every time: **tense** (shift?), **person** (who is 'I' now?), **pointers** (here/now/tomorrow).
*Di + infinitive* is the safe, natural choice for commands; *che + congiuntivo* sounds more formal.
In speech, if what was said is still true, Italians often skip the shift (*Ha detto che è stanca*). In writing, shift.

exercises.instruction: Report the sentence. Complete with the correct form.
exercises.prompt: «Sono stanca.» → Ieri sera Anna mi ha detto che ___ (essere) stanca.

traps.why: Past reporting verb + a statement about that moment: presente → imperfetto, *era*.
Her tiredness was at the time she spoke, not later: *era*.
*Dire che* reporting a statement takes the indicative.

exercises.explanation: Presente → **imperfetto** after a past reporting verb.
exercises.en: Last night Anna told me she was tired.

exercises.instruction: Report the sentence. Complete with the correct form.
exercises.prompt: «Arriverò alle dieci.» → Giulio ha scritto che ___ (arrivare) alle dieci.

traps.why: Futuro → condizionale **passato** in reported speech: *sarebbe arrivato*.
The reporting verb is past (*ha scritto*): the future shifts to *sarebbe arrivato*.

exercises.explanation: Futuro → **condizionale passato**.
exercises.en: Giulio wrote that he would arrive at ten.

exercises.instruction: Report the sentence. Complete with the correct form.
exercises.prompt: «Ho perso le chiavi.» → Mia sorella mi ha detto che ___ (perdere) le chiavi.

traps.why: Passato prossimo → **trapassato** after a past reporting verb: *aveva perso*.
She lost them *before* speaking: trapassato, not condizionale passato.

exercises.explanation: Passato prossimo → **trapassato prossimo**.
exercises.en: My sister told me she had lost her keys.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct reported form.
exercises.prompt: «Chiudi la porta!» → Il professore mi ha detto ___ la porta.

optionWhy.0: The imperative can't stay in reported speech.
optionWhy.2: *Che chiudo* reports a statement ('that I close'), not a command.

exercises.explanation: Command → **di + infinitive**.
exercises.en: The teacher told me to close the door.

exercises.instruction: Report the sentence, shifting the time expression.
exercises.prompt: «Torno domani.» → La settimana scorsa Piero ha detto che sarebbe tornato ___.
answers: (il giorno dopo|il giorno seguente|il giorno successivo|l'indomani)

traps.why: He spoke last week, so his 'tomorrow' is not our tomorrow: *il giorno dopo*.
*Il giorno prima* replaces *ieri*. For *domani* use *il giorno dopo*.

exercises.explanation: *Domani* → **il giorno dopo / l'indomani** when reported on a different day.
exercises.en: Last week Piero said he'd be back the next day.

exercises.instruction: Report the question.
exercises.prompt: «Hai fame?» → Mia nonna mi ha chiesto ___ avessi fame.

traps.why: Reported yes/no questions are introduced by *se* ('whether/if').
That's Spanish! Italian 'if' is *se*.

exercises.explanation: Yes/no question → **se**.
exercises.en: My grandmother asked me if I was hungry.

exercises.instruction: Put into reported speech, starting with 'Luisa disse che…'.
exercises.prompt: «Sono qui da un'ora.»
answers: Luisa disse che era (lì|là) da un'ora

traps.why: *Qui* is the speaker's place: in reported speech it becomes *lì / là*.
Past reporting verb: *è* → *era*.
Luisa is now 'she': third person *era*.

exercises.explanation: Present → imperfetto; *qui* → **lì**.
exercises.en: Luisa said she had been there for an hour.

exercises.instruction: Put into reported speech, starting with 'Marco mi ha chiesto…'. (You're reporting it a week later.)
exercises.prompt: «Chiamami stasera!»
answers: Marco mi ha chiesto (di chiamarlo|che lo chiamassi) quella [stessa] sera

traps.why: «Chiamami» means 'call **him**' (Marco): the pronoun becomes *lo* → *di chiamarlo*.
A week later, *stasera* is no longer tonight: *quella sera*.
The imperative becomes *di* + infinitive.

exercises.explanation: Command → *di chiamarlo*; *stasera* → **quella sera**.
exercises.en: Marco asked me to call him that evening.

exercises.instruction: Put into reported speech, starting with 'Il poliziotto mi ha chiesto…'.
exercises.prompt: «Dove abita?»
answers: Il poliziotto mi ha chiesto dove (abitavo|abitassi)

traps.why: Past reporting verb and you are now the subject: *dove abitavo* (or formal *abitassi*).
Wh-questions keep the question word (*dove*); *se* is only for yes/no questions.

exercises.explanation: Wh-question → keep *dove*; present → **abitavo / abitassi**.
exercises.en: The police officer asked me where I lived.

exercises.instruction: Put into reported speech, starting with 'Carla mi disse che…'. (Reported weeks later.)
exercises.prompt: «Domani porterò mia figlia dal medico.»
answers: Carla mi disse che (il giorno dopo|il giorno seguente|il giorno successivo|l'indomani) avrebbe portato sua figlia dal medico
Carla mi disse che avrebbe portato sua figlia dal medico (il giorno dopo|il giorno seguente|il giorno successivo|l'indomani)

traps.why: *Mia figlia* (Carla's) → *sua figlia* in reported speech.
Weeks later, *domani* → *il giorno dopo / l'indomani*.
Futuro → condizionale passato: *avrebbe portato*.

exercises.explanation: Three changes: **avrebbe portato**, **sua**, **il giorno dopo**.
exercises.en: Carla told me she would take her daughter to the doctor the next day.

exercises.instruction: Put into reported speech, starting with 'La guida ci ha detto…'.
exercises.prompt: «Non toccate niente!»
answers: La guida ci ha detto (di non toccare|che non toccassimo) niente

traps.why: The imperative becomes *di non* + infinitive.
Reported commands use *di* + infinitive or *che* + congiuntivo imperfetto (*toccassimo*).

exercises.explanation: Negative command → **di non toccare** (or *che non toccassimo*).
exercises.en: The guide told us not to touch anything.

exercises.instruction: The teacher was speaking to you. Report it, starting with 'L'insegnante mi disse che sperava…'.
exercises.prompt: «Spero che tu abbia capito.»
answers: L'insegnante mi disse che sperava che [io] avessi capito

traps.why: Congiuntivo passato → congiuntivo **trapassato** after a past reporting verb: *avessi capito*.
You are now reporting about yourself: *che (io) avessi capito*.
The teacher was speaking to **you**: first person *avessi*.

exercises.explanation: Congiuntivo passato → **trapassato**; *tu* → *io*.
exercises.en: The teacher told me she hoped I had understood.

exercises.instruction: Translate into Italian.
exercises.prompt: He asked me whether I had seen the film.
answers: [Lui] mi (ha chiesto|chiese|ha domandato|domandò) se (avevo|avessi) visto il film

traps.why: «Hai visto?» → *se avevo visto* (trapassato) after a past reporting verb.
Yes/no question → *se*, not *che*.

exercises.explanation: Yes/no question → *se*; passato prossimo → **avevo / avessi visto**.
exercises.en: He asked me whether I had seen the film.

exercises.instruction: Translate into Italian.
exercises.prompt: She told us to wait outside.

traps.why: A reported command becomes *di* + infinitive: *di aspettare*.
*Dire* + infinitive takes *di*, not *a*: *ci ha detto di aspettare*.
'Us' as indirect object = *ci*, placed before the verb: *ci ha detto*.

exercises.explanation: Command → **di aspettare**.
exercises.en: She told us to wait outside.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct form. Watch the reporting verb.
exercises.prompt: «Partirò domani.» → Ogni volta che lo vedo, Luca dice che ___ domani.

optionWhy.1: The reporting verb is **present** (*dice*): no shift.
optionWhy.2: No shift with a present reporting verb.
optionWhy.3: *Dire che* reporting a statement takes the indicative.

exercises.explanation: Present reporting verb → tenses stay as they were: **partirà**.
exercises.en: Every time I see him, Luca says he's leaving tomorrow.

exercises.instruction: Put the words in order.
exercises.prompt: She asked me if I wanted to stay for dinner.
answers: Mi ha chiesto se volessi restare a cena
exercises.explanation: Reported yes/no question: *se* + congiuntivo imperfetto (formal) or imperfetto (*volevo*).

exercises.instruction: Report the sentence, shifting the time expression.
exercises.prompt: «Ci rivediamo qui la settimana prossima.» → Il mese scorso Dario ci aveva detto che ci saremmo rivisti lì ___.
answers: (la settimana dopo|la settimana successiva|la settimana seguente)

traps.why: Reported a month later: *la settimana prossima* → *la settimana dopo / successiva*.
*La settimana prima* replaces *la settimana scorsa*.

exercises.explanation: *La settimana prossima* → **la settimana dopo / successiva**.
exercises.en: Last month Dario had told us we'd meet there again the following week.

exercises.instruction: Say it in Italian.
exercises.prompt: Your flatmate was out when the landlord called this morning. Tell her: "He said he would come by tomorrow to fix the boiler."
answers: Ha detto che (sarebbe passato|passerà) domani a (riparare|sistemare) la caldaia
Ha detto che domani (sarebbe passato|passerà) a (riparare|sistemare) la caldaia

traps.why: Same day: his 'tomorrow' is still tomorrow, so *domani* stays.
'Would come by' after a past verb → *sarebbe passato* (or *passerà*, since tomorrow is still ahead).

exercises.explanation: Same day → *domani* stays. *Sarebbe passato* is standard; *passerà* is fine because the event is still in the future.
exercises.en: He said he'd come by tomorrow to fix the boiler.

exercises.instruction: Write 60–100 words in Italian.
exercises.prompt: Report a recent conversation (with a boss, a friend, a doctor…). What did they tell you, ask you, and tell you to do? Use reported speech only, no quotation marks.

rubric.label: Reports a yes/no question with se
Reports a command with di + infinitive
Shifts the tenses (imperfetto, trapassato or condizionale passato)
rubric.hint: *Ha detto che era…, che aveva…, che avrebbe…*

rubric.label: No quotation marks
rubric.hint: Reported speech only: no direct quotes.

exercises.model: Ieri il mio capo mi ha chiamato nel suo ufficio. Mi ha chiesto se avevo finito la relazione per il cliente e io gli ho detto che mi mancava ancora un capitolo. Allora mi ha detto di consegnarla entro venerdì e di non preoccuparmi per il resto. Ha aggiunto che la settimana dopo saremmo andati insieme a Torino e che lì avrei presentato il progetto. Mi ha anche chiesto quando sarei andato in ferie.
exercises.explanation: Past reporting verbs, *se* for questions, *di* + infinitive for commands, shifted tenses and pointers.
